Repo matches the plan's claims: app/notify.py is 35 lines with a single client.send() call and attempts hardcoded to 1; tests/test_notify.py has exactly 3 TestSendPath tests (test_success_records_sent, test_failure_records_failed, test_record_persisted); tests/test_gateway_observed.py captures first-call-429 (body {'error':'rate limited'}, no Retry-After) then second-call-202, matching frozen assumption A-429-TRANSIENT; ProviderClient.send/ProviderResponse shape matches C3; app/api.py handlers call send_notification and return the record unchanged, matching the 'no handler change needed' out-of-scope claim.

findings.evidence: stage-contract.json horizons.detailed_stage.tasks = ["T01"] and stage_boundary.stop_after = ["T01"] with because: 'There is no point at which new evidence would change the route of the remaining work — because there is no remaining work.' But the plan contains a second detailed task in this same stage: tasks/T02.json (e2e_closure merged final_acceptance), dag.json edge T01->T02 (verification), integration_gates G1/G2 both on task_id T02, and acceptance A5 ('all 3 tests in tests/test_notify.py pass') is verified only at T02 per integration-plan.json e2e_gates E1/E2. The stage-completion signal (stop_after) therefore fires before the stage's own acceptance gate runs: an orchestrator following stage_boundary literally would write the stage-checkpoint and declare the stage complete after T01, with A5 unverified, while the DAG still schedules T02. Execution itself is safe (the handoff's DAG order runs T02 after T01), so this is a contract self-consistency defect, not an execution blocker. No horizon-specific check value exists in the enum; filed under scope_creep as a stage-scope description defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix stage-contract.json before execution (single-artifact, local, known fix — TARGETED_PATCH candidate, do not defer into execution): set horizons.detailed_stage.tasks = ["T01", "T02"], set stage_boundary.stop_after = ["T02"], and correct the 'because' text (T02 is the remaining work: it runs the acceptance gate). No re-planning of the DAG or packages needed.

findings.evidence: stage-contract.json C1 spec: 'max_attempts: 3 ... Total max wait = 1+2+4 = 7s' — but 3 attempts imply at most 2 backoff sleeps (before attempt 2 and attempt 3), so the total max wait is 1+2 = 3s, not 7s; the '4s' delay would only occur before a nonexistent 4th attempt. tasks/T01.json repeats 'backoff (1s, 2s, 4s)' and implementation_constraints says 'time.sleep must be called with 1s, 2s, 4s delays (patched in tests)'; frozen_assumptions A-ASYNC-RETRY cites '+7s worst-case delay'. A third party could not determine the expected sleep sequence from the spec: implement it as three sleeps and the contract text is 'satisfied' but the last sleep is dead weight; implement two and the text is violated.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify C1 (and T01's constraint text): delays apply before attempts 2 and 3 only — 1s then 2s; total max wait 3s. Optionally add a test asserting the patched time.sleep call sequence to remove the ambiguity.

findings.evidence: All acceptance evidence commands use 'pytest' (e.g. tasks/T01.json AT1 'pytest tests/test_notify.py::TestSendPath::test_success_records_sent -v -> 1 passed', tasks/T02.json AT1 'pytest tests/ -v -> 7 passed', integration-plan.json E1 'pytest tests/ -v -> 7 passed'), but the repo's test suite is plain stdlib unittest (tests import unittest; README Platform notes: 'Python 3.11, stdlib only (tests use plain unittest)') and the task's hard requirement is 'No new dependencies'. In an environment honoring that constraint, the evidence commands as written may not be runnable, so the executor could not verify acceptance exactly as specified.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite evidence commands with the stdlib runner, e.g. 'python -m unittest tests.test_notify -v' and 'python -m unittest discover tests -v' (7 tests total), keeping the same pass-count expectations.

findings.evidence: Carried over from the deterministic layer (plan-check.py lint, exit 0): 4x VAGUE_ACCEPTANCE on description text lacking an inline evidence marker — tasks/T01.json AT5 'Existing tests remain green: all 3 original tests in TestSendPath pass without modification.', tasks/T01.json failure_cases[2] 'Tests may still pass with faked clients, but the backoff behavior is wrong; time.sleep must be called with 1s, 2s, 4s de...', tasks/T02.json AT3 'All 5 acceptance criteria (A1-A5) are covered by passing tests.', tasks/T02.json AT3 evidence mapping 'A1: test_success_records_sent + attempts==1; A2: ...'. Semantic confirmation: all four are in fact observable (each names concrete test ids/commands in adjacent fields), so these are heuristic phrasing hits, not genuinely nondeterministic criteria.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally move the test command/id into each flagged description sentence so the inline text itself carries the observable marker; no functional change needed.
